menu.tagline: It has waited for you longer than you think.
menu.story: You wake in an abandoned psychiatric clinic. The power is out — without it there is no calling the lift down to the basement, and the basement is the only way out. It is somewhere close. Find fuses, fix the panels, and try not to shine your light into the dark.

floor0.title: WARD No. 9 — Residential Block
floor0.intro:
The power went out years ago. To call the elevator down,
you need to restore power to the fuse box. Find 3 fuses.
floor0.descend_text: THE ELEVATOR SLOWLY DESCENDS INTO THE BASEMENT...
floor1.title: WARD No. 9 — Basement
floor1.intro:
This is where it lives. Three valves control the steam
for the old surface hatch — without them, it won't budge.
floor1.descend_text: THE HATCH LEADS UP TO THE OPEN AIR...
floor2.title: WARD No. 9 — Backyard
floor2.intro:
The yard is fenced in, barbed wire along the top. Past it lies the forest.
The shed holds a pair of cutters, but two padlocks hang on the door.
Find 2 keys to get inside.
note.floor0.0:
"...patients from Block B were moved downstairs again. Dr. Krein forbade
asking why. The lights in Corridor B have been flickering for three weeks
straight, and the electricians still haven't come..."
note.floor0.1:
"Duty log, night 14: Patient No. 9 doesn't appear in any admission
records. Staff insist he's always been here. We stopped going down to the
basement."
note.floor0.2:
"The panel in the store room is dead. Someone has torn the wires out three
times now. Someone badly does not want the lift going down. I do not know
who. I do not want to find out."
note.floor0.3:
"Shift report, 03/14: the patient in Ward 12 complained again about ‘the
one that crawls in the pipes.’ The orderlies have been laughing at that
story for six months. I don't find it funny at all."
note.floor0.4:
"Ward directive: being in Corridor B after lights-out without an escort is
strictly forbidden. No reason is given in the order."
note.floor0.5:
"Someone chalked on a locker door: ‘IT COUNTS YOUR STEPS.’ We erased it,
of course. It was back the next day, in the same handwriting."
note.floor0.6:
"Personal file: Patient No. 9 was admitted without a referral, without
relatives, without a birth date. The ‘diagnosis’ field is blank. We should
have asked who brought him here."
note.floor0.7:
"The new nurse quit after her third night shift. All she said was:
‘Someone answers when you call the patients by their names. It isn't
them.’"
note.floor0.8:
"3 a.m. rounds. Ward 9 is empty, door locked from the outside. As always.
As if he was never there at all — just a name on the plate."
note.floor0.9:
"...they're moving patients downstairs in batches, like they're clearing
the floor. Nobody wants to say what for."
note.floor0.10:
"Third month running, the drug store writes off enough sedative for a ward
twice our size. Dr. Krein signs the forms without reading them. I asked
who it was all for, and I was moved to another floor."
note.floor0.11:
"I counted the wards. The register lists four more than the corridor has.
Not closed, not under repair — they are simply not there. And somehow
nobody but me notices."
note.floor0.12:
"N. and I made a pact: if one of us does not come back from a shift, the
other does not go looking. No exceptions — we both promised. Tonight it is
my turn not to go."
note.floor0.13:
"Dr. Krein does not age. I have been here eleven years, and the photograph
in his file is exactly the same man. I am thirty-four and I look fifty."
note.floor0.14:
"Third week running we are told to ‘clear’ the wards in the far wing.
There is nothing to clear: what is in them has not been patients for a
long time. We open the door, leave a trolley at the threshold and do not
go in."
note.floor0.15:
"The kitchen has gone to two shifts: staff are fed here now, and almost
nobody goes home. Temporary, they say, until the end of the quarter. The
camp beds have been in the hall since March."
note.floor1.0:
"If you're reading this — don't keep your light on for long. It comes for
the light faster than it comes for sound. I thought it was the other way
around. I was wrong, once."
note.floor1.1:
"These valves hold back something the manual has not one line about.
Someone opened them and wrote down no reason. Shut them behind you on your
way out. If you get out at all."
note.floor1.2:
"The boiler room hasn't run since winter, but someone comes down to check
it every night. That name isn't on the shift log."
note.floor1.3:
"It's colder down here than it should be with the heating running. We
checked the pipes three times. The pipes are fine."
note.floor1.4:
"Sign on the utility corridor door: ‘AFTER 22:00 — TWO PEOPLE, NOT ONE.’
Someone scrawled underneath in marker: ‘IT DIDN'T HELP ANYWAY.’"
note.floor1.5:
"The basement inventory was halted by orders from above. The last entry in
the log cuts off mid-sentence."
note.floor1.6:
"We stopped going for the old equipment in the far power block. Easier to
write off the inventory than go down there as two and come back as one."
note.floor1.7:
"The cage in the corner of the utility bay was here before us. In the
records, it isn't listed as medical equipment, or as anything else."
note.floor1.8:
"If the vent hum stops, do not work out why. Just run upstairs. I worked
it out once. I will not again."
note.floor1.9:
"Someone welded the grate over the old crawlspace in the wall before I
ever got here. It wasn't welded shut to keep us out."
note.floor1.10:
"They take the bodies out of the basement morgue at night, and not one
removal is on paper. The register says we have twelve places. Tonight I
counted seventeen of them occupied."
note.floor1.11:
"Sheets come back from the laundry with stains that no temperature takes
out. The matron told us to stack those apart and not ask questions."
note.floor1.12:
"I have stopped keeping the register. There is no point: what comes down
from upstairs matches no ledger, and what goes out matches nothing that
came in. These two months I have only been signing."
note.floor1.13:
"Something answers from the cold store if you call a name. I tried it
twice, to be sure. I will not be trying it again."
note.floor1.14:
"The rooms at the far end of the basement are listed as an isolation
block. No doctor goes down there; the keys are held by orderlies with
clearance. Mine was taken last month, and I did not ask why."
note.floor2.0:
"The fence has been repaired three times this month. From the outside, not
the inside — like something's trying to get in, not out."
note.floor2.1:
"The second lock on the shed is there for a reason. The first was for
thieves. The second went on after the cutters disappeared — and then
turned up back in their place, like nobody had ever touched them."
note.floor2.2:
"The forest past the fence isn't part of the hospital grounds on any
official map. That land has been down in the register as ‘unaccounted for’
for forty years."
note.floor2.3:
"Escape attempt, night of July 9th: the patient made it to the gap in the
fence. He was found in the morning ten meters from it, facing the
building, not the forest."
note.floor2.4:
"The watchmen were formally forbidden to patrol the yard after midnight.
The written order gives no reason — only the time."
note.floor2.5:
"Staff belongings turn up on the barbed wire on the forest side sometimes.
Not torn to shreds, not dropped in the mud — hung up neatly, like they're
on display."
note.floor2.6:
"We keep the cutters in the shed instead of with security on purpose. If
it wants someone to leave through that gap — that decision shouldn't be
its to make."
note.floor2.7:
"The yard is lit worse than the building, even though the wiring is newer
and up to current code. The lamps in the far corner burn out faster than
the rest — the same ones, every time."
note.floor2.8:
"The yard chapel is locked, and the candles inside still burn down by
morning. There is one key, and it hangs at the guard post. Nobody takes
it."
note.floor2.9:
"Nothing has grown in the greenhouse since last spring — not a weed, not
even mould. The soil is warm all the same, as if it had just been turned.
The gardener quit without collecting his pay."

editor.help.1.title: VIEWS
editor.help.1.body:
Tab — toggles CAMERA <-> GRID (flat top-down view).
Unavailable during test floor generation.
editor.help.2.title: FREE CAMERA
editor.help.2.body:
WASD moves, SPACE up, LEFT CTRL down, LEFT SHIFT faster.
All of it works ONLY while the right button is held — which is also
how you look around. Let go and the keyboard is the editor's again.
editor.help.3.title: TOOLS (right panel)
editor.help.3.body:
Furniture — click places the chosen piece where its ghost is drawn
under the cursor (Alt: the middle of the cell). Q / W / E / M switch
what the mouse does: CURSOR (place), MOVE, TURN, MAGNET.
In MOVE and TURN a click picks the PIECE rather than the cell, and a
piece standing ON another wins — so the tray comes off the counter
rather than the counter under it.
MOVE: the dot in the middle is free; the red arrow is X only, the
green one Y only, the orange one the diagonal; dragging the piece
itself is free too. TURN: drag the ring, any angle.
R turns a quarter, with SHIFT 15 degrees, with CTRL the other way; the
mouse wheel does the same. DEL/BACKSPACE removes.
A wall piece does not turn: it faces out of its wall, and turning it
means moving it to another wall. Pipes sit in the middle of their cell
and do not move — remove one and place it again.
Whatever stands ON a piece moves and turns with it.
A wall piece cannot be pulled off its wall: it has one arrow, along
the wall, and a hanging one (sconce, sign, extinguisher) a blue one
up as well; CTRL + wheel changes its height too. MAGNET: clicks pick
pieces, Enter squares them to the wall and closes the row, Esc clears.
Keys 1..9 pick a tool.
Wall / Window / Bars / Eraser — can be dragged with LMB held, paint or
erase cells one at a time. A window is a wall material and
needs at least one floor cell next to it. Bars can be seen and
lit through but not walked through; floor they shut in is
hatched — nothing spawns there, but furniture can be placed.
Doors — click a room border to place/remove a door.
In yard-zone mode interior doors work the same way, and
the zone's border is painted with the Wall/Eraser tool.
editor.help.4.title: DOORS
editor.help.4.body:
A door on the room's border docks with the neighbouring room when the floor is generated; a door inside the room is an interior one. Where it stands says which — there is nothing to mark.
Kind: opening — no leaf; door — a normal door; broken — torn off its hinges; random — the generator picks one of the three.
editor.help.5.title: WEIGHT AND REQUIRED FURNITURE
editor.help.5.body:
Generator weight — the higher it is, the more often the generator
picks this room among rooms of the same kind.
exit/unlocker rooms must contain exactly 1 item of the required
kind — it's highlighted in orange.
editor.help.6.title: FILE
editor.help.6.body:
New room / Open list / Save (blocked while there are
errors) / Validate — the same check without saving.
editor.help.7.title: TEST-GENERATE A FLOOR
editor.help.7.body:
Assembles a real floor out of ALREADY-SAVED rooms/zones — unsaved edits to the current one don't participate.
The generator closes dead-end corridors with the nearest
fitting room itself, and can dock neighboring rooms even
without an exact door match, as long as both have a door
on the right side — sometimes with two passages at once.
editor.help.8.title: OTHER
editor.help.8.body:
The mode button in the right panel toggles Room <-> Yard zone.
ESC — exit test generation, otherwise close the editor.
